title: Prove the sharp inverse envelope under a column cap (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the sharp inverse 1-norm envelope for every complex n by n matrix E with absolute row sums at most rho and column sums at most m rho, where 0<rho<1 and integer m>=2.

```text
exact maximum ||(I-E)^-1||_1 = sum_(i=1)^n rho^ceil(log_m i) / (1-rho)
attainment: E_(i,ceil(i/m)) = rho, every other entry zero
critical case n=m^h, rho=1/m: exact maximum h+m/(m-1)
```

Claim type: scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. The bound covers diffuse rows and arbitrary complex phases. Sorted inverse-column partial sums supply the upper bound; one explicit nonnegative routing matrix attains it. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

This takes the abstract column-budget portion of Ali Romman's #5255 open conditioning question. The predecessor's row-only theorem is a cited premise for comparison, not a replay deliverable. At row cap 1/2, adding column cap 1 changes the dimension-8 maximum from 9 to 5 and the dimension-64 maximum from 65 to 8. These compare different admitted matrix classes.

## Task and overlap

Only six files in `research/column-capped-resolvent/` are added. Base is `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8. TASK.json explicitly changes `complex-rank-shape-decoder` to this conditioning side result. Source definition, selected record and original card are pinned as provenance; there are no external runtime inputs.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19440639). Live claims, current/open account work, main README object/formula searches and merged searches were checked before commitment. The cached snapshot covered 734 open PRs and 6,839 Discussion records with complete remote pagination. Sparse local-note coverage was incomplete, supplemented by main-tree Git searches. Unpublished work remains outside coverage.

## Evidence and reproduction

Local CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

- All 6,144 admitted half-row-unit matrix evaluations through dimension three pass exact rational inversion and 54,072 partial-sum inequalities. The exact maximum is attained in all 18 parameter domains. Another 648 signed matrix evaluations exercise cancellation.
- All 2,240 attaining fixtures through dimension 64 pass 72,800 column equations and 72,800 transport equalities; 420 also have separately computed dense inverses. Sixteen critical closed forms, twelve rejected inputs and five contract/example controls pass.
- Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized commands pass with identical full generated receipts. Individually timed local checks take 3.94 and 3.99 seconds, below their 180-second limits. These are timeout observations, not a performance comparison.
- Registered replay, exact committed bytes, modes and source-history preflight pass at `c1d915303450bec823784befd3ada5a261796a5c`.
- Official export and input coverage pass. Both modes pass from a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH and PYTHONPATH. All seven exported files, including the manifest, stay unchanged; full receipts agree and their six package hashes match the committed blobs.
- In-memory compilation, AST function-size inspection and staged whitespace checks pass. The largest function is 34 lines; a separate static linter is unavailable.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/column-capped-resolvent/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/column-capped-resolvent/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/column-capped-resolvent
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/column-capped-resolvent --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Other hosts may substitute their Python 3.12 path. Expected markers are `PASS_COLUMN_CAPPED_RESOLVENT`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The verifier writes no files and prints a generated receipt bound to all package hashes. The written proof establishes the unbounded theorem; finite enumeration corroborates it.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

No actual emitted Gaussian matrix is admitted to these caps. Physical preparation, rounding, stock, native operations, ownership/restoration, tapes, compiler, analytic recovery and the complete supplier invoice remain separate. All five selected assumptions remain. Arbitrary noninteger column-to-row ratios, unequal row caps and prescribed supports are outside this theorem.

Every registered check ran locally. No predecessor scientific suite, selected cold replay, native suite, Lean or Docker build ran. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Determine the exact envelope for a noninteger column-to-row ratio. Begin with a three-vertex rational-cap transport problem allowing split rows; integer parent routing does not saturate fractional capacities.
- Bind both caps to one exact emitted Gaussian coefficient matrix and charge its preparation. That matrix and physical cost are the missing steps toward a precision improvement.

## Related open work

- #6459 sharpens a constant-shift Gaussian inverse spectral-norm bound. This gives an exact induced 1-norm maximum over an abstract row/column-cap class; no common numerical inverse norm is computed.
- #6483 determines a fixed-rank approximation asymptote for a varying-phase Gaussian inverse. This provides no approximation spectrum or source-specific Gaussian bound.
- #6671 gives sharp Euclidean conditioning for ordered square-zero error words. This concerns a single resolvent under simultaneous absolute-sum constraints and does not extend that word model.

- #6790 proves a bounded-error rank cutoff for acyclic decoder rows using a triangular comparison envelope. This theorem optimizes a resolvent 1-norm under simultaneous row and column caps; it computes no decoder error cutoff.
- #6794 improves a sufficient three-qubit Clifford tensor-Gram condition bound. That spectral-norm matrix family differs from this abstract resolvent 1-norm class; no common numerical norm is computed.

The related-work refresh inspected all ten open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM, including this PR. The other nine, #6785 through #6794 excluding #6788, compute no competing value for this simultaneous-cap envelope. The adjacent conditioning results are distinguished above. No additional computations were run to check other contributors' results.

## Credit

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman #5255 for the support-envelope theorem and column-budget question, plus #5306 for unequal row budgets; Cinna Davis #4100 and James Reed #4282 for the conditioning/periodic-section context; Nick Petalas #5859 for the distinct forbidden-diagonal extension; and ToikY #4209 for same-rho Schur closure. Neumann comparison, transport inequalities and partial-sum induction are classical. General literature priority is unclaimed. All predecessor credit remains unchanged. Apache-2.0.
